rich.text: — ויפגע במקום וילן שם כי בא השמש ויקח מאבני המקום: “He encountered the place and lodged there, for the sun had set.” The whole os is built on the three clauses of this verse — the encounter (prayer and cleaving), the lodging (the night prayer), and the setting sun (Yaakov himself).

paragraphs.text: Genesis 28:11 — ויפגע במקום וילן שם כי בא השמש ויקח מאבני המקום: “He encountered the place and lodged there, for the sun had set.” The whole os is built on the three clauses of this verse — the encounter (prayer and cleaving), the lodging (the night prayer), and the setting sun (Yaakov himself).

rich.text: — כי בא השמש רבנן אמרי … מלמד שהשקיע הקדוש ברוך הוא גלגל חמה שלא בעונתה בשביל לדבר עם יעקב אבינו בצנעה: the Sages read “for the sun had set” as an early sunset God brought about in order to speak with Yaakov privately, like a king who has the lamps put out to speak with his friend alone. Rav Tzadok uses this first reading to show that, on its terms, “for the sun had set” explains the lodging (he was compelled to stop), which the second reading does not.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 68:10 — רבי פינחס בשם רבי חנין דצפורין אמר שמע קולן של מלאכי השרת אומרים בא השמש בא השמש אתא שמשא אתא שמשא, בשעה שאמר יוסף והנה השמש והירח אמר יעקב מי גלה לו ששמי שמש: Yaakov heard the angels announcing “the sun has come,” and years later, when Yosef dreamed of “the sun and the moon” (Genesis 37:9), he said, “Who revealed to him that my name is Sun?” The print's ר"פ is Rabbi Pinchas, as in the Midrash.

rich.text: — רבי שלמוני בשם ריש לקיש אמר תרכוסא של שלש רגלים הראה לו. רבי יהושע דסכנין בשם רבי לוי אמר את הוא רגל שלישי … כי חלק ה' עמו יעקב חבל נחלתו, מה החבל הזה פחות משלשה אין מפקיעין אותו, כך האבות אין פחות משלשה: in the dream God showed Yaakov a three-legged stool, and Yaakov is its third leg; as a cord of fewer than three strands does not hold, so the Patriarchs are not fewer than three. Rav Tzadok reads this as the revelation that Yaakov completes the Chariot, the answer to his question about the angels' “Sun.”

rich.text: — כי חלק ה' עמו יעקב חבל נחלתו: “For Hashem's portion is His people; Yaakov is the cord of His inheritance” — the verse the Midrash expounds as the three-stranded cord of the Patriarchs.

paragraphs.text: Deuteronomy 32:9 — כי חלק ה' עמו יעקב חבל נחלתו: “For Hashem's portion is His people; Yaakov is the cord of His inheritance” — the verse the Midrash expounds as the three-stranded cord of the Patriarchs.

rich.text: (Rav Tzadok) — quotes the same Midrash (ב"ר פ' סח: מה החבל הזה פחות מג' אין מפקיעין אותו) and explains it as here: יעקב כולל קדושת אברהם ויצחק, citing the Zohar (I 207a) דיעקב תושבחתא דאבהן איהו. It adds that Yaakov's inclusiveness is the attribute of truth (תתן אמת ליעקב), the “threefold cord” that is not quickly broken, and applies it to a Shabbat that falls on Rosh Chodesh Chanukah.

rich.text: — רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: תְּפִלּוֹת אָבוֹת תִּקְּנוּם. רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: תְּפִלּוֹת כְּנֶגֶד תְּמִידִין תִּקְּנוּם: “The prayers — the Patriarchs instituted them,” against the view that they correspond to the daily offerings; the Gemara concludes that the Patriarchs instituted them and the Sages linked them to the offerings.

p: from the words “And he encountered the place” (Berachos 26b).
That is: even when a person is in darkness,
so that he cannot see the light of His holiness
even so there will avail him
so that he merits to see light
This is what it says, “And he encountered the place [HaMakom]”:
to the Holy One, blessed be He,
he is, as it were, truly
the light of the Holy One, blessed be He.
And this is what it says, “and he lodged there”:
that he instituted the evening prayer
“Who revealed to him that my name is Sun?”
And this is what it says afterward:
which they expounded in the Midrash Rabbah (parashah 70):
“From the wrath of the Holy One, blessed be He,
and they said in the Midrash Rabbah:
and to merit a great light.

Rav Tzadok explains why the night prayer belongs to Yaakov: prayer in the dark, when the light of His holiness cannot be seen.
